name: Laft-Gourzin-Bandar Abbas Gas Pipeline

values.OtherEnglishNames: Bandar Abbas-Laft-Gourzin Gas Transmission Line; Bandar Abbas-Qeshm Gas Pipeline; Bandar Abbas-Laft-Gavrzin (Qeshm) Gas Pipeline
values.RouteNotes: Corridor: Bandar Abbas (Hormozgan mainland) -> Bandar Pol, then a ~3 km subsea HDD crossing of the Persian Gulf at ~70 m depth to Bandar Laft on Qeshm Island, continuing to Gourzin. Subsea crossing described as a first for Iran's gas industry. No official GIS route located.

researcher_notes: New row. No existing GEM Iran gas row covers Qeshm Island / Laft / Gourzin (checked all 42 rows in discovery_context; nearest, North-Northeast P6026 ending 'Shahid Babaei Expressway', is a separate Bandar Abbas-area line). Add-threshold met: (a) sponsor = Iran Gas Engineering and Development Company (IGEDC), the state gas developer/executor and NIGC subsidiary; asset owner/operator = National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), which lists the line among its commissioned gas lines in the FY1403 roundup; (b) endpoints = Bandar Abbas (Hormozgan mainland) -> Bandar Pol -> subsea crossing -> Bandar Laft -> Gourzin, Qeshm Island; (c) concrete step = construction complete/partly commissioned. CONFIRMED FACTS (consistent across 4 sources): 59 km total, 30 in transmission line; ~3 km subsea HDD crossing at ~70 m water depth from Bandar Pol to Bandar Laft, billed as the first subsea crossing for Iran's gas industry; supplies Qeshm industries, Persian Gulf industrial park, power plants and residents. STATUS: set 'operating' - Tehran Times/NIGC FY1403 roundup (year to Mar 2025) says 37 km commissioned with further expansion planned; offshore-mag (Jun 2025) reports the subsea crossing completed; PressTV (Jan 2026) frames the crossing as completed. IranOilGas (Nov 2025) still called the full line 'nearing completion', so a human reviewer may prefer 'construction' for the un-commissioned remainder; the built/commissioned portion is in service, hence 'operating'. CAPACITY unknown (left blank). Confidence: high on physical attributes (length/diameter/subsea/endpoints agree across independent trade press offshore-mag + IranOilGas Network and NIGC state reporting). Independence caveat: some coverage traces to Shana (Iranian state wire), but offshore-mag and IranOilGas Network are independent trade editorial. Owner set to NIGC (reuse existing 'National Iranian Gas Co' entity); IGEDC is developer/executor. Route: no official GIS found; corridor described in RouteNotes, RouteAccuracy=approximate - candidate for a human routes-repo lookup, do not fabricate coords.
